```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
library(here)
library(tidyverse)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

t2 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "table_2_avg_effect_by_primary.csv"),
               show_col_types = FALSE)
txt <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "text_sample_and_weighting.csv"),
                show_col_types = FALSE)
fig1 <- read_csv(here("maintained", "output", "figure_1_thresholds_by_primary.csv"),
                 show_col_types = FALSE)

cell <- function(topic_key, party_name, quantity) {
  rows <- str_detect(t2$Topic, fixed(topic_key)) & t2$Party == party_name
  stopifnot(sum(rows) == 1)
  t2[[quantity]][which(rows)]
}

group_n <- function(quantity_name) {
  value <- txt$value[txt$quantity == quantity_name]
  stopifnot(length(value) == 1)
  formatC(value, format = "d", big.mark = ",")
}

# The change-format share of a group saying more or less likely, as the panel plots it.
panel_share <- function(group, sign_value) {
  rows <- fig1$primary_party == group & fig1$topic == "docs" & fig1$sign == sign_value &
    str_trim(fig1$measure) == "Change" & fig1$threshold == -0.01
  stopifnot(sum(rows) == 1)
  sprintf("%.1f", 100 * fig1$P[which(rows)])
}

pp <- function(x) sprintf("%.1f", x)
pv <- function(x) sprintf("%.3f", x)
```

```{r entries}
# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from this tibble into
# this document and into the machine-readable errata_entries.csv written at the bottom of
# the file, which is what any other document carrying these corrections reads. Before the
# spine existed an entry was written out in prose wherever it was needed, and the copies
# had already diverged.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here. Nothing else in a field is markup, so the same string can be set by any of them.
#
# Numbering follows PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b: entries are ordered by severity block (quantity;
# description, interpretation, definition; label, float, cross_reference; wording, spelling,
# typography; bibliographic), discovery order inside a block, and a finding that lands in an
# earlier block renumbers the entries after it. Renumbered 2026-11-07; the old-to-new map is
# in that day's commit message.
#
# A published or corrected value that the pipeline computes stays computed: the field is
# built with str_glue() so the number is produced when this document renders, not typed.
#
# claim_ids is the semicolon-separated list of ground-truth claim_id values the entry
# corrects, and it is what makes "is this finding published?" a query rather than a reading
# of every note. It is empty where an entry has no ground-truth row, which is normal for a
# bibliographic or structural entry. ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R refuses to build if
# any id here is absent from the ground truth.
#
# corrected_values runs parallel to claim_ids, one value per id in the same order, carrying
# the corrected quantity as a number rather than as a sentence. Each value is built from the
# same expression that builds the marked span of the corrected sentence, so the two cannot be
# written apart, and the gate below re-checks that each one is still inside its span. An
# entry that changes no quantity carries NA. A value is the number without the sentence's
# sign or label, so "+1.8" carries 1.8 and "p = 0.05" carries 0.05.
cv_belief_pp <- pp(cell('Believe', 'Neither', 'cf_diff'))
cv_belief_p  <- pv(cell('Believe', 'Neither', 'cf_p'))
cv_vote_pp   <- pp(cell('general election', 'Neither', 'cf_diff'))
cv_vote_p    <- pv(cell('general election', 'Neither', 'cf_p'))
cv_rep_p     <- pv(cell('primary election', 'Republican', 'cf_p'))
cv_n_neither <- group_n('n_primary_neither')
cv_n_rep     <- group_n('n_primary_republican')
cv_n_dem     <- group_n('n_primary_democratic')

entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The counterfactual estimates for respondents intending neither primary",
  "p. 1222",
  "By contrast, the counterfactual format suggests indifference: these respondents report that the indictment slightly revised their beliefs in favor of the idea that Trump mishandled documents ([[+1.8]] pp, s.e. = 0.9, [[p = 0.05]]), with no substantial effect on vote choice ([[+0.1]] pp, s.e. = 0.9, [[p = 0.89]]).",
  str_glue("By contrast, the counterfactual format suggests indifference: these respondents report that the indictment slightly revised their beliefs in favor of the idea that Trump mishandled documents ([[+{cv_belief_pp}]] pp, s.e. = 0.9, [[p = {cv_belief_p}]]), with no substantial effect on vote choice ([[+{cv_vote_pp}]] pp, s.e. = {pp(cell('general election', 'Neither', 'cf_se'))}, [[p = {cv_vote_p}]])."),
  paste("Table 2 already prints all four corrected values. The two standard errors quoted in",
        "the sentence are right, so the estimates were not computed on a different sample; the",
        "four wrong figures appear only here."),
  paste0("text_p_1222_neither_primary_effect_on_belief_pp;",
         "text_p_1222_neither_primary_effect_on_belief_p_value;",
         "text_p_1222_neither_primary_effect_on_general_election_vote_pp;",
         "text_p_1222_neither_primary_effect_on_general_election_vote_p_value"),
  str_c(cv_belief_pp, ";", cv_belief_p, ";", cv_vote_pp, ";", cv_vote_p),

  2, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The p-value for the effect on Republican primary vote",
  "p. 1222",
  "Republican primary voters also thought that the indictment made them less likely to vote for Trump in the primary: on average, they reported a 64.1 percent chance of doing so, compared with 65.7 percent if the indictment had not been issued (difference = 1.6 pp, s.e. = 0.6, [[p = 0.02]]).",
  str_glue("Republican primary voters also thought that the indictment made them less likely to vote for Trump in the primary: on average, they reported a 64.1 percent chance of doing so, compared with 65.7 percent if the indictment had not been issued (difference = 1.6 pp, s.e. = 0.6, [[p = {cv_rep_p}]])."),
  str_glue(
    "Table 2 prints {pv(cell('primary election', 'Republican', 'cf_p'))} for the same ",
    "estimate. The estimate and its standard error are stated correctly, and the finding is ",
    "significant at conventional levels on either figure."),
  "text_p_1222_republican_primary_voters_effect_on_primary_vote_p_value",
  cv_rep_p,

  3, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "Figure 1's caption reports the wrong group sizes",
  "p. 1224, Figure 1 caption",
  "Figure 1a displays results for respondents who did not plan to vote in either primary (N = [[754]]). Figure 1b and 1c displays results for those who plan to vote in the Republican primary (N = [[2,026]]) and Democratic primary (N = [[1,953]]).",
  str_glue("Figure 1a displays results for respondents who did not plan to vote in either primary (N = [[{cv_n_neither}]]). Figure 1b and 1c displays results for those who plan to vote in the Republican primary (N = [[{cv_n_rep}]]) and Democratic primary (N = [[{cv_n_dem}]])."),
  str_glue(
    "The three published figures are the counts of respondents by partisan identity, not by ",
    "intended primary: {group_n('n_party_id_independent')} respondents identify as ",
    "Independents, {group_n('n_party_id_republican')} as Republicans and ",
    "{group_n('n_party_id_democrat')} as Democrats. They are the group sizes of figure A.1."),
  paste0("figure_1_caption_n_respondents_intending_neither_primary;",
         "figure_1_caption_n_republican_primary_voters;",
         "figure_1_caption_n_democratic_primary_voters"),
  str_c(cv_n_neither, ";", cv_n_rep, ";", cv_n_dem),

  4, "float", "pipeline", "full",
  "Figure 1's panels are printed in the wrong order",
  "p. 1224, Figure 1 caption",
  "Figure 1a displays results for respondents who did not plan to vote in either primary (N = 754). [[Figure 1b]] and [[1c]] displays results for those who plan to vote in the Republican primary (N = 2,026) and Democratic primary (N = 1,953).",
  "[[figure 1 is reprinted below]] with its panels in the order the caption and the body text describe. Nothing plotted differs.",
  str_glue(
    "The panel printed as **(b)** is the Democratic one. Its belief column shows ",
    "{panel_share('Democratic', 1)} per cent of respondents saying more likely against ",
    "{panel_share('Democratic', -1)} per cent saying less likely, and its vote column is the ",
    "general election, which only respondents outside the Republican primary were asked ",
    "about. The panel printed as **(c)** is the Republican one, with a belief split of ",
    "{panel_share('Republican', 1)} per cent more likely against ",
    "{panel_share('Republican', -1)} per cent less likely and a Republican primary vote ",
    "column. The body text carries the same assignment as the caption and so points at the ",
    "wrong panel twice, at \"In figure 1b, huge fractions of Republican primary voters report ",
    "that the indictment made them think it was 'less likely' Trump mishandled documents\" ",
    "and at \"We see this same basic pattern (reversed) among Democratic primary voters in ",
    "figure 1c.\""),
  "figure_1_panel_b_shows_republican_primary_voters_1_yes;figure_1_panel_c_shows_democratic_primary_voters_1_yes",
  NA_character_,

  # Entries 5-7 are decision 6's kind: no error is too small. All three were
  # found by the remastered edition's R10, which renders the published page and
  # this edition's beside each other, and none of them is a quantity, so none
  # carries a claim_id.
  5, "typography", "reading", "brief",
  "A missing space after a colon",
  "p. 1217",
  "the approach ameliorates the response substitution [[problem:rather]] than having",
  "the approach ameliorates the response substitution [[problem: rather]] than having",
  paste("The colon runs into the word after it. This could not be settled from the published",
        "text layer, which returns the same string whether the page sets a space the extractor",
        "drops or sets none: the RENDERED page prints no space, so it is what the page sets."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  6, "bibliographic", "reading", "brief",
  "The CBS News URL prints a space where a hyphen belongs",
  "p. 1232",
  "see-security-risk-after-[[trump indictment/]]",
  "see-security-risk-after-[[trump-indictment/]]",
  paste("A space is not a character a URL can carry, so the address as printed is not an",
        "address. Both halves are on one line of the published page, so the space is the",
        "page's own and not a line break the extractor left behind. With the hyphen restored",
        "the address resolves. Entry 7 is the same defect in the FiveThirtyEight entry on the",
        "page after."),
  "",
  NA_character_,

  7, "bibliographic", "reading", "brief",
  "The FiveThirtyEight (2023b) URL prints a space where a hyphen belongs",
  "p. 1233",
  "say-after-trumps-[[second indictment/]]",
  "say-after-trumps-[[second-indictment/]]",
  paste("The same defect as entry 6, one page later and in the second of the article's two",
        "FiveThirtyEight references. Both halves are on one line of the published page, and",
        "with the hyphen restored the address resolves."),
  "",
  NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values), as.character))

# A count is stored as a plain number, without the sentence's thousands separators.
entries <- entries |>
  mutate(corrected_values = str_remove_all(corrected_values, "(?<=\\d),(?=\\d{3})"))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
# The column and the sentence are written from one expression, so they begin in agreement
# and this gate exists for the edit that separates them: a value moved from one marked span
# to another, a span reworded to carry a second number, a claim id appended without its
# value. Each value has to be inside the span it belongs to, matched by position where the
# counts line up, and inside SOME span where an entry marks a label as well as a number and
# its spans outnumber its values.
# Thousands separators are dropped from a span, since the column stores plain numbers.
marked_spans <- function(x) {
  str_remove_all(str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2], "(?<=\\d),(?=\\d{3})")
}

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values)) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, \(v, s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

# A quantity entry that corrects something has to say which quantity, and an entry that
# corrects none (any other class, or a note) may not carry a value. The class is the
# declaration and this is where it binds. An empty claim_ids counts as missing.
has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & nzchar(entries$claim_ids)
no_value_ok <- integer()
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" &
                                        has_ids & !entries$entry %in% no_value_ok])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity" | entries$form == "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# Every id an entry claims to correct must be a real ground-truth claim. The build gate in
# ground_truth/build_ground_truth.R checks the same property from the other side; checking it
# here too means a dangling id cannot survive a render.
gt_ids <- read_csv(here("ground_truth", "barari_etal_2024_ground_truth.csv"),
                   show_col_types = FALSE)$claim_id
cited_ids <- entries$claim_ids |>
  str_split(";") |>
  unlist() |>
  str_trim() |>
  discard(\(x) is.na(x) | x == "")
stopifnot(all(cited_ids %in% gt_ids))

# The prose below counts the entries in words, as the note has always done.
n_entries_word <- c("one", "two", "three", "four", "five", "six", "seven", "eight", "nine",
                    "ten", "eleven", "twelve")[nrow(entries)]

# The spine's markup, resolved for this document.
bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

This note lists `r n_entries_word` errors in "Did Trump's Indictments Rally His Base? Evidence from the Counterfactual Format," published in *Public Opinion Quarterly* 88(4), doi [10.1093/poq/nfae061](https://doi.org/10.1093/poq/nfae061). **None of them changes a conclusion of the paper.** They are recorded because a reader who followed the text to a panel, or quoted one of the numbers, would be misled.

Items 1 and 2 are sentences that disagree with the article's own table 2. Item 3 is a caption reporting the wrong group sizes. Item 4 is a figure whose panels are printed in an order the caption and the body text do not describe. Items 5 to 7 are typographic: a colon run into the word after it, and two reference URLs printed with a space where a hyphen belongs, neither of which is an address a reader can follow. Every corrected value below is computed from the deposited replication archive ([10.7910/DVN/QDOBJF](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/QDOBJF)) at the time this document is rendered. The maintained code is at [github.com/active-maintenance-aec/barari_etal_2024](https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/barari_etal_2024).

```{r entries-1-3, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so every emitted entry opens
# with one.
emit <- function(i) {
  e <- entries[i, ]
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ",
      str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
      "\n\nCorrected:\n\n> ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
}
walk(which(entries$entry <= 3), emit)
```

```{r entry-4, results="asis"}
# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so every emitted entry opens
# with one. This entry's corrected artifact is the float printed beneath it rather than a
# token, so its corrected field is set as a sentence and its markers are stripped.
e <- entries |> filter(entry == 4)
cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\nPublished, ", str_remove(e$location, "^published "), ":\n\n> ",
    bold(e$published), "\n\n", e$note, "\n\nCorrected: ",
    str_remove_all(e$corrected, "\\[\\[|\\]\\]"), "\n", sep = "")
```

```{r remaining-entries, results="asis"}
walk(which(entries$entry >= 5), emit)
```

```{r emit-spine}
# The machine-readable spine, written wherever this document is rendered. Anything else that
# carries these corrections reads it rather than keeping its own copy, so the two cannot drift.
# The spine's vocabularies are closed (cleanup of 2026-11-07): a value outside them is a
# typo, and the edition builders read these columns to shape every entry.
stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
